what:
Cursor adapter audience-mapping pattern (decided 2026-04-27 — REVISED with empirical constraint discovered in same-day testing).

**Verified mapping (Claude Code → Cursor):**
- Claude Code `systemMessage` (user-visible chrome) ↔ Cursor `user_message` ONLY when paired with `permission:"deny"` or `continue:false`. **Empirical 2026-04-27: under `permission:"allow"` or in events without permission (stop, beforeSubmitPrompt without continue:false), Cursor accepts user_message in the hook JSON but does NOT render it in chat.** ANSI-stripping doesn't fix this — the field is ignored regardless.
- Claude Code `additionalContext` / `decision:block.reason` ↔ Cursor `agent_message`. Reaches agent context regardless of permission value. ✅ verified empirically (agent acted on stored conventions returned via agent_message).

**REVISED scenario shapes (post-empirical 2026-04-27):**

| Scenario | Cursor shape (verified working) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Hard block (preToolUse deny) | `{permission:"deny", user_message:<chrome>, agent_message:<agent-instruction>}` | Both fields render ✅ |
| Soft nudge (preToolUse allow) | `{permission:"allow", agent_message:<agent-instruction>}` | user_message accepted but **not rendered** under allow → drop it. Chrome cannot surface to user on soft preToolUse in Cursor 3.2.11. |
| Stop reprompt | `{followup_message:"<chrome-prefix> — <agent-instruction>"}` | user_message accepted but **not rendered** on stop → prefix chrome into followup_message instead. |
| beforeSubmitPrompt block | `{continue:false, user_message:"<chrome> — <reason>"}` | Use prefix pattern OR rely on user_message rendering with continue:false (untested; default to prefix for safety). |
| Standalone systemMessage | empty (no user-visible channel for non-deny chrome) | Could prefix into surrounding event instead — or drop. |

**Key constraint to remember:** Cursor's `user_message` is bound to permission:"deny" / continue:false rendering. It's not a general-purpose chat-channel under "allow." This is a verified Cursor 3.2.11 behavior — not documented in cursor.com/docs/hooks but empirically confirmed. Track as forum FR if desired.

**Implication for soft preToolUse user-visibility:**
- Cursor users do NOT see "aide-memory · prompting aide_search" chrome on soft nudges
- Claude Code users DO see it (systemMessage renders inline)
- This is a genuine Cursor platform gap that survives the audience-mapping fix
- Mitigation: rules-file injection (`alwaysApply:true`) covers static guidance; per-event chrome on soft paths is uncovered. Could prefix chrome into agent_message so agent surfaces it organically in its response — explore as fast-follow if user-visibility on soft turns out to matter.

**Why the prior version of this memory was wrong:** I claimed "user_message=chrome works under allow" based on Cursor docs listing user_message as a preToolUse field without restriction. The docs don't specify the allow-vs-deny rendering rule. Per directive #358: docs-listing-the-field ≠ field renders in all cases. Need empirical verification, which we now have.

**Stop hook prefix pattern (per the revised mapping):**
- Current emit (post-this-fix): `{followup_message:<reason>, user_message:<chrome>}` — user_message ignored
- Revised emit: `{followup_message:"<chrome> — <reason>"}` — chrome prepended into the only-rendered field
- Still feels less polished than Claude Code's separate systemMessage but is the actual user-visible path on Cursor.
why: User empirically tested both the soft preToolUse (B+ adversarial) and stop hook with chrome — Cursor renders user_message under deny but NOT under allow or stop, even though the JSON is accepted without error. Updating the design memory to reflect the verified constraint. The bias-correction directive (#358) was right that we should default to capability parity, but verified absence is verified absence — Cursor genuinely doesn't render user_message in non-deny paths in 3.2.11.
